title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling and in‑flight request draining
description: Provides production‑grade process termination by listening to SIGTERM/SIGINT, stopping new connections, and waiting for active requests to finish or timeout. This prevents dropped requests and resource leaks during deployments or container restarts.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a request is in progress and verify the server stops accepting new connections but allows the in‑flight request to complete before exit
Trigger SIGINT with no active requests and ensure the server shuts down immediately and process.exit is called with code 0
acceptance:
- Server registers listeners for SIGTERM and SIGINT
- New connections are rejected after signal receipt
- In‑flight requests are allowed up to a configurable timeout (default 10 s)
- Process exits with code 0 on successful shutdown, non‑zero on timeout
- Logs appropriate shutdown steps without uncaught exceptions
reason: Ensures reliability during automated deployments and container orchestrations, reducing 5xx errors caused by abrupt termination and aligning the framework with production best practices.
